text: The Lord Lewis Prize is presented by the Royal Society of Chemistry to recognize outstanding and distinguished achievements in chemistry or science, as well as significant contributions to science policy. The recipient is awarded a medal, a certificate, and a prize of £5,000. The prize is given every two years in honor of Professor Lord Lewis's substantial contributions to chemistry and science policy. The first recipient of the Lord Lewis Prize was Lord May of Oxford, who served as former president of the Royal Society and chief scientific advisor to the UK Government, and received the award in 2008.
